title: Splitflow: Simulated traffic sculptor and guided rollback walkthrough
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Design a guided ‘Splitflow’ experience in the Redwood Console that lets engineers preview, simulate, and rehearse traffic splits (canary / A/B) and run a guided rollback rehearsal before live traffic is changed. The intent is to reduce accidental regressions and shorten mean-time-to-recover by making rollouts more predictable and rehearsable. This ticket covers low-fidelity flows, an interactive prototype for simulation mode, and a walkthrough for operations and SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype demonstrates: create a traffic split, simulate requests over a time range, visualize latency/cost/quality overlays, and perform a simulated rollback that updates the timeline and metrics.
Hand-off artifacts include annotated Figma frames, a flows document describing states and edge cases, and a PRD section for product/eng handoff.
Design validated with PM and two backend engineers; feedback items captured and triaged.
Accessibility review checklist completed for the main controls (contrast, keyboard focus, aria labels).
reviews: 2025-02-20 design sync: PM (Maya Patel) suggested adding a cost-delta preview for each split variant.
2025-02-24 eng review: Backend (Ravi Gupta) flagged edge-case where KV cache warmup skews simulated latency; suggested overlay label and a toggle to include/exclude warmup phase.
2025-02-28 security review: preliminary OK; security asked that simulated logs avoid exfiltrating customer PII (design will mask request payloads in simulation).
progress_notes: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after kickoff with PM and SRE. Initial user stories drafted.
2025-02-19: Sketches for 'drag-to-sculpt' traffic editor and 'what-if' timeline completed.
2025-02-21: Built low-fidelity prototype showing timeline scrubber and confidence bands for metrics.
2025-02-26: Added cost preview widgets per-variant; iterated on microcopy to clarify simulated vs. live state.
2025-03-04: Incorporated QA notes from accessibility pass; preparing handoff package.
decisions: Simulated mode will run against anonymized telemetry snapshots, not live traffic. This reduces blast radius and simplifies compliance.
Rollback rehearsal will be represented in UI as a reversible timeline operation that can be exported to a rollout plan JSON for the backend to execute.
We will show a 'confidence band' for each metric (p50/p90/p99) for simulated requests rather than single-line predictions to surface uncertainty.
Cost delta estimates will be surfaced as an hourly and 30-day projection per-split variant to help product owners weigh trade-offs.
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for timeline scrubber and slider-based traffic sculptor; aria-live region for critical alerts.
